The Earth's temperatures (post-Cambrian Explosion) occurred about 50 million years ago, shortly after that last of the dinosaurs died off. Around 25 million years ago, ice formed in the Antarctic. Around 3 million years ago, camels first appeared in what is modern day Canada. They obviously migrated to warmer climates as the Earth continued to cool. Around 2 million years ago, ice formed in the Arctic, and the current Ice Age began. This is also when modern humans appeared on the scene.

During the Ice Age, there are glacial periods and inter-glacial periods. The glacial periods last around 250,000 years, on average, and ice moves from the Arctic to much of the Northern Hemisphere (but not Siberia, oddly). Then, the ice recedes during the inter-glacial periods. This is what we are living in today.

The current inter-glacial period began around 10,000 years ago, which is also when the large animals that early man hunted went extinct. They could not survive the warmer temperatures. So, man had to learn how to adapt, which is why man began to figure out agriculture at around that time.

The average inter-glacial period lasts about 10,000 years, so we are due for a return to the glacial period at any time. And researchers have determined that glacial periods can come on very quickly -- within 10-20 years sometimes.
